Bonds provide a form of financial protection against damages. A bond is a binding agreement executed by a bidder or vendor and another party to guarantee the performance of certain obligations or duties to the purchaser. There are three types of bonds that may be appropriate for inclusion in procurement for costly items or construction projects.
(Ord. No. 2013-018, art. 3, intro. ¶, 11-25-2013)
134:
Bid bonds provide surety that the firm awarded a bid shall not withdraw the bid, shall insure the execution of the contract document, and shall furnish any required payment and performance bonds. When specified in the bid package, each bid must be accompanied by a bid bond of not less than five percent of the amount of the bid where the cost is greater than $100,000.00, or as required by the city. The guarantee may be in the form of a cashier's check or certified check made payable to the City of Emerson, or a bid bond issued by a surety company. Bid bonds will be returned upon award of the contract.
(Ord. No. 2013-018, art. 3, § 1, 11-25-2013)
135:
A performance bond is executed subsequent to award by a successful bidder to protect the city from loss due to the bidder's inability to complete the contract as agreed, and to secure the fulfillment of all contract requirements. When specified in the bid package, the successful bidder will be required to furnish a performance bond prior to commencing work. The guarantee of performance may be in the form of a cashier's check, certified check made payable to the City of Emerson, performance bond, or irrevocable letter of credit issued by a bank or savings and loan association as defined in O.C.G.A. ch. 7-1A. Irrevocable letters of credit will not be accepted on contracts of more than $300,000.00.
(Ord. No. 2013-018, art. 3, § 2, 11-25-2013)
136:
The successful bidder will be required to furnish a guarantee of payment for the protection of all subcontractors, individuals, or businesses participating in the project or contract. The payment bond is normally in the amount of the contract awarded and must be provided prior to commencing work. This bond is required for construction or other projects with subcontractors when specified in the bid package. This guarantee may be in the form of payment bond, cashier's check, certified check made payable to the City of Emerson, or an irrevocable letter of credit issued by a bank or a savings and loan as defined in O.C.G.A. § 7-1-4. Irrevocable letters of credit will not be accepted on contracts of more than $300,000.00.
(Ord. No. 2013-018, art. 3, § 3, 11-25-2013)
137:
When required in the bid package or by other regulation, a maintenance bond will be provided in the amount and for the length of time as specified in the bid package.
(Ord. No. 2013-018, art. 3, § 4, 11-25-2013)
140:
A vendor confirmation or a city purchase order establishes the specific items and requirements of the ordering department. There is a departmental follow-up responsibility to see that the goods or services received match what was ordered. Specifically, when goods are received, the order should be inspected and compared to both the packing slip that accompanies the order and the purchase documentation. The receiving verification should also provide assurance that the goods arrived in good condition. Any discrepancies in quantity or condition should be noted on the purchase documentation and must be satisfactorily resolved prior to payment. Similarly, any services performed under contract should be verified for completion and correctness prior to payment. Each department is responsible for establishing its own internal procedures to ensure accountability for this function. The packing slip should be retained with the purchase documentation.
(Ord. No. 2013-018, art. 4, § 1, 11-25-2013)

The state department of administrative services maintains statewide contracts on many commodities and services. Many of these contracts are available for use by local governments. Using this source for purchases can save time and money. Since state contracts are already the result of a competitive process, departments are authorized to purchase off of state contracts at the prices bid or negotiated by the state in lieu of requirements for obtaining additional competitive prices. Nevertheless, departments are encouraged to spot check state contract prices with prices available for the same item from another source in an effort to obtain the most favorable price.
(Ord. No. 2013-018, art. 4, § 2, 11-25-2013)
142:
(a) "Only known source" purchases are purchases of goods or services that are so unusual or unique that only one vendor is known to provide this item. Departments must take care to avoid eliminating competition by writing specifications in such manner that needlessly and unfairly results in elimination of sources of supply.

(Ord. No. 2013-018, art. 4, § 3, 11-25-2013)

(a) Normal competitive purchasing procedures may be temporarily waived during bona fide emergencies. (b) The city manager must declare a "state of emergency" that would permit a waiver of normal purchasing procedures. Departments shall still use such competitive procedures as circumstances reasonably permit. Emergency purchasing provisions must not be used to compensate for poor planning.

(a) It is often advantageous to procure goods or services on an annual or long-term basis. Such procurement might be for service or maintenance contracts, or for the purchase of commodities such as building or office supplies or petroleum products. Service or maintenance contracts typically specify a term (length of agreement).
(b) Purchase of commodities may result in a pricing agreement. For example, a vendor might offer a percent discount from catalog or list price in anticipation of selling a greater quantity of goods to the city. Where competition exists, pricing agreements can be sought through either the less formal quotation process or the more formal bid process. Pricing agreements should require no commitment on the part of the city to buy a specific quantity of goods or services, and should contain a non-exclusive clause that allows the city flexibility to use other vendors when needed or desired. In the event that the city enters into any pricing agreements, the city shall confirm the arrangement through a blanket purchase order which would confirm the pricing agreement but not specify specific quantities of goods to be purchased. The city clerk shall maintain a file of any blanket purchase orders.
(c) Normally, no contracts or blanket purchase orders shall exceed one year in length.
(Ord. No. 2013-018, art. 4, § 5, 11-25-2013)
145:
Purchase of a brand name product or service is permissible when the goods comprise a major brand system, program, or service previously selected by the city. This is allowed only when operational effectiveness, future enhancements or additions, or maintenance and storage of spare parts preclude the mixing of brands, manufacturers, etc.
(Ord. No. 2013-018, art. 4, § 6, 11-25-2013)
146:
For the procurement of services where the qualifications of the firm or its principals are central to the services performed, the initial step may be the issuance of a request for qualifications (RFQ). RFQs are typically used when a specialized professional service is sought. An RFQ might seek information regarding the background of the firm, summaries of similar work done by the firm, references, biographies of the personnel that would be used, time requirements, etc. Cost estimates are not normally sought in an RFQ process. Once RFQs have been received and evaluated, the top candidates might be invited for interviews and/or to provide price bids.
(Ord. No. 2013-018, art. 4, § 7, 11-25-2013)
147:
Purchases made at the end of one fiscal year and beginning of the next fiscal year can cause confusion regarding which budget is used for the purchase. This is not a matter of choice or discretion. Generally accepted accounting principles for local governments provide that expenditures take place when the liability is incurred. In other words, if a purchase order is issued in June, the amount of the purchase order is charged against that year's budget, even if the item is not received until July or August. On the other hand, generally accepted accounting principles do not permit a purchase initiated in July to be charged against the prior year's budget. To reduce end-of-year confusion and accounting problems, year-end purchasing should be kept to a minimum.
(Ord. No. 2013-018, art. 4, § 8, 11-25-2013)

Supporting documentation includes quotation forms for medium amount purchases and purchase orders for purchases greater than $2,500.00, invoices, receipts, check request forms, credit card statements, expense reports, etc.
(b) Payment authorizations should be supported by original invoices rather a copy of an invoice or a statement. This is important to prevent duplicate payments to vendors. Any exceptions must be documented explaining the reason for using a copy.
(c) Payment checks to vendors shall not be issued by the city clerk until the department head or other authorized department employee has approved the invoice or other supporting document for payment.
(d) The city's standard terms of payment are to pay within 30 days of the receipt of an invoice. All city staff must work together to ensure that this standard is met.
(e) Approval of invoices is part of each department's fiscal accountability. This step is intended to ensure that no checks are issued merely because an invoice has been received. Department heads or other staff authorized to approve invoices shall carefully check the invoices and assure themselves that the goods have been received in good condition and in the correct quantity (or that the service has been satisfactorily performed), prior to approving payment. Invoices should be returned to the city clerk within three to five business days. Any charges in dispute shall promptly be communicated to the vendor. The department head or authorized staff reporting the dispute shall then await resolution prior to payment.
(f) Special handling and rush handling of invoices is inefficient and expensive. Therefore, priority must be given to standard, efficient invoice processing according to established procedures, and avoid invoice handling outside of the norm.
(g) Invoices occasionally provide an early payment discount (for instance, two percent of the payment price may be deducted if the invoice is paid within ten days). Such invoices should be expedited to ensure that the city loses no discounts.

(Ord. No. 2020-012, § 1, 9-28-2020)
195:
The mayor and city council, in making its determination on an application, shall be guided by the following factors as to whether or not to issue or deny a license under this chapter:
(1) No license shall be granted to any person, unless such person is at least 21 years of age.
(2) A license application may be denied to any applicant for a license where it appears that the applicant would not have adequate financial participation in the proposed business to direct and manage its affairs, or where it appears that the applicant is intended to be a mere surrogate for a person who would not otherwise qualify for a license for any reason whatsoever.
(3) No employee or official of the city shall be eligible to receive a license.
(4) The city may require all applicants to provide financial statements and other evidence of financial responsibility in conjunction with the application.
(5) All applicants for a license shall meet all requirements or qualifications of the appropriate licensee as described in this chapter.
(6) No license shall be granted to an applicant who does not meet all requirements or qualifications of the appropriate licensee as described in this chapter.
(7) An applicant shall be active in the operation of the licensed business and shall be personally present on the licensed premises sufficiently to assure compliance with the provisions of this chapter. For purposes, a licensee shall not be considered active unless he is an owner, stockholder, or fulltime employee of the licensed business and is present on the licensed premises a minimum of ten hours per week.
(8) A license issued to an individual shall be issued in the name of the individual. A license issued to a partnership shall be issued in the name of the partnership and in the name of the partner or employee primarily responsible for the operation of the licensed premises who shall be the named licensee. A license issued to a corporation shall be issued in the name of the corporation and in the name of the stockholder, officer of the corporation, or employee primarily responsible for the operation of the licensed premises who shall be the named licensee. A license issued to a purely nonprofit civic, fraternal, patriotic, private, or social club or corporation which is organized and conducted in the city solely as a mutual benefit membership group, shall be issued in the name of the club or corporation and in the name of the individual primarily responsible for the club or corporation's compliance with this chapter, and the named individual shall be named licensee.
(9) The individual completing and presenting an application for a license, whether for himself, a partnership, a corporation, or a nonprofit organization shall meet the requirements of this chapter so as to be the named licensee.
(10) No license shall be issued for any location which is not in compliance with the city zoning or building ordinances.
(11) Approval of an application shall expire after 90 days from the date of such approval, unless the applicant has procured and paid the fee for the approved license. The mayor and city council may extend the approval up to 90 days for cause, provided the request therefor is made within the original 90 days.
(12) No applicant may submit, and the mayor and city council shall not act upon, an application which is substantially the same as an application submitted within the previous six months, unless the mayor and city council exercises its discretion to do so.
(13) The mayor and city council may defer action upon any application, the subject matter of which is substantially the same as the subject matter of litigation then pending in state or federal courts, until such time as the litigation is resolved.
(14) Whenever the mayor and city council shall deny an application for a license, the applicant shall have 15 days following notification of denial to request a hearing before the mayor and city council. The applicant shall be entitled at such hearing to present evidence and cross-examine opposing witnesses present at the hearing.
(15) The applicant must be present at the meeting of the mayor and city council at which his application is considered. If the applicant is not present, the mayor and city council cannot consider the application and may table it until the next meeting or deny it, which requires the applicant to resubmit and pay any required fees again (fees are not refunded if the application is denied).
(16) The nature of the neighborhood immediately adjacent to the proposed location, that is, whether the same is predominately residential, industrial or business.
(17) The proximity of churches, hospitals, schools, college campuses, public libraries, public parks and playgrounds, private residences and alcoholic treatment centers owned and operated by the state or any county or municipal government therein.
(18) Whether the proposed location has adequate off-street parking facilities or other parking available for its patrons.
(19) Whether the location would tend to increase and promote traffic congestion, and resulting hazards therefrom.
(20) The criminal record of the applicant and the outlet manager and general good character and reputation and his financial responsibility; provided that nonpayment of federal, state, county or city taxes shall be prima facie evidence of lack of financial responsibility.
(21) A report from the city manager, chief of police, the building inspector, the fire marshal or city engineer.
(22) The information required in the application or statement, and whether all requirements as to notice, advertisements, fire codes, building, zoning, parking, lighting and legal matters have been met.
(23) Evidence as presented to the council for or against the application.
(24) Whether or not the granting of the application is in the interest of the city.
(25) Whether any license for sale or beer or wine or alcohol previously issued for the location has been revoked for cause by the city.
(26) Whether the applicant holds or possesses any other license for the sale of alcohol issued by the city.
(27) The history or reputation of the building or establishment (proposed for an outlet) for prostitution or other sex offenses, fighting, shooting, stabbing or other violence, gambling, illegal dealing in alcoholic beverages or drugs, and other violations of the law.
(28) Compliance with the requirements of this chapter and the provisions of the Code.
(29) If a licensee has failed to satisfy the criteria for obtaining a license to sell.
(30) If a licensee, or such licensee's employee or agent, has violated any federal, state, or local laws of ordinances relating to the use and sale of drugs and alcoholic beverages, and/or violent crimes.
(31) When the continued operation of the licensed business is determined to be detrimental to the health safety, or welfare of the public.
(32) The failure of the licensee or his employees to report immediately to the city a known violation of law or municipal ordinances, breach of peace, disturbance or altercation occurring in or in the immediate proximity to the licensee's premises.
(33) Failure by the licensee to adequately supervise and monitor the conduct of the employees, patrons and others on the licensed premises, including, but not limited to, adjacent parking lots or areas which may be lawfully used by patrons of the licensed establishment, in order to protect the safety and well-being of the general public and of those utilizing the premises.
(34) In breach of the peace, disorderly conduct or altercations and incidents involving breach of the peace, disorderly conduct, or altercations, the following additional factors shall be considered:
a. The facts and circumstances of the incident.
b. The parties involved.
c. The criminal history of the parties, if any.
d. Damage to persons and property.
e. Intoxication levels of individuals involved.
f. Conduct of employees and the licensee in regards to said incident and involvement.
g. Mitigating circumstances.
(Ord. No. 2020-012, § 1, 9-28-2020)
196:
A licensee under this chapter must be and continue to be a person of a good moral character, be a resident of the United States for a period of at least one year, and must meet the following additional qualifications, which shall be required during the entire period that the licensee shall hold the license.
(1) The applicant shall not have been convicted, within five years of the date of his application, of a felony or any violation of the laws of this state or any other state relating to the sale of alcoholic beverages.
(2) The applicant shall not have had revoked, for cause, such as a violation of regulations or improper operation, within three years next preceding his application, any license issued to him by any state, county, or municipality to sell alcoholic beverages. This subsection shall not apply to any licenses heretofore revoked by the city.
(3) The applicant must not have any past due city taxes, bills, fees, assessments or any other charges.
(4) All applicants must be at least 21 years of age.
(5) The applicant must be able to read and write the English language.
(6) The applicant shall make a sworn statement of his qualifications under subsections (1) through (5) of this section and shall place it on file with the city before any license is issued. Any misstatement or concealment of fact in the application shall be grounds for revocation of the license and shall make the applicant liable to prosecution for perjury under the laws of the state.
(7) The applicant may not employ any person who does not meet the employee qualifications as outlined in this chapter.
(8) A violation of any of the above qualifications and restrictions shall be grounds for suspension or revocation of the license issued.
(Ord. No. 2020-012, § 1, 9-28-2020)
197:
No application for a pouring license shall be granted to an applicant whose premise for a pouring outlet is anything other than a restaurant, hotel, motel, private club, or lounge, as defined in this chapter. It is the intention of this chapter that wine and malt beverages for consumption on the premises be sold only at bona fide restaurants, hotels, motels, and private clubs under the restrictions herein set out, and not at walk-in bars or sham establishments; provided, however, any property within a city-approved CID which includes both a sand volleyball venue of six or more courts and a multi-purpose indoor sports facility of not less than 125,000 square feet shall be permitted a pouring license for wine and malt beverages for consumption on the premises within the confines of the indoor facility, volleyball venue, baseball complex or soccer complex, and upon compliance with divisions 1, 2 (excepting this section), 3, and 4 (excepting sections 4-191, 4-192, and 4-193) of this article.
(Ord. No. 2020-012, § 1, 9-28-2020)
198:
Any wholesaler of malt beverages or wine licensed by the state or the agent of such wholesale dealer may be granted a license to distribute such beverages in the city upon application for such license to the city and presentation of evidence that he understands this chapter and the conditions under which retail licenses are issued.
(Ord. No. 2020-012, § 1, 9-28-2020)
201:
Licenses issued under this chapter shall be displayed prominently at all times on the premises for which same was issued.
(Ord. No. 2020-012, § 1, 9-28-2020)
202:
(a) A license issued under this chapter shall be subject to all terms and conditions imposed by this chapter or any future ordinance. License holders shall be responsible for compliance with such terms and conditions by all of their employees and those working under their supervision and control. It shall also be the duty of the license holder and those under his supervision and control to report to the city any violation of this chapter occurring on the premises of the license holder.
(b) All licenses shall have printed on the front the following language:
"This license is granted by the city council and accepted by licensee subject to all of the terms and conditions of the ordinances governing the issuance and retention of the same."
(Ord. No. 2020-012, § 1, 9-28-2020)
203:
In case of revocation, the licensee shall not be entitled to a refund of any license fee paid.
(Ord. No. 2020-012, § 1, 9-28-2020)
204:
(a) Licenses suspended for a definite period shall be automatically reinstated without further hearing after the definite period has elapsed.
(b) Licenses suspended pending compliance with designated conditions to be corrected shall be automatically reinstated upon compliance, without further hearing.
(Ord. No. 2020-012, § 1, 9-28-2020)
205:
Immediately upon the sale or closing of a business licensed under this chapter, the licensee shall surrender his license to the city.
(Ord. No. 2020-012, § 1, 9-28-2020)
206:
A licensee shall make immediate report to, and receive approval by, the council of any change in the interests in or ownership of the pouring outlet and any change in the information as stated in the original application for license, including the list of employees.
(Ord. No. 2020-012, § 1, 9-28-2020)
207:
In the event of death or termination or resignation of any employee or other person holding a license, there shall be a 30-day grace period for the owner of the business engaging in the sale of alcoholic beverages to obtain a new license from the city.
(Ord. No. 2020-012, § 1, 9-28-2020)
208:
Licenses issued pursuant to the provisions of this chapter shall not be transferable.
(Ord. No. 2020-012, § 1, 9-28-2020)
209:
(a) All licenses shall be issued on a calendar year basis and shall be renewable as a matter of course upon payment of the appropriate fee, on or before December 31 of each year, except as otherwise provided in this chapter.
(b) The license fee shall be paid in full.
(c) The city shall provide the chief of police with a list of current license holders prior to the annual renewal date. The chief of police shall report on the licensee's activity, if any, and upon activity at the location of the licensed business, if any, during the year.
(d) If the chief of police reports any activity which constitutes probable cause for not renewing a license, the renewal shall not be made, and the matter shall be referred to the mayor and city council for its consideration.
(e) The mayor and city council shall afford the licensee a public hearing, after reasonable notice, and in passing upon the application for renewal, the mayor and city council shall be guided by the same criteria and qualifications for issuance of the initial license.
(f) At the public hearing, the mayor and city council may grant or deny for cause the renewal of any license.
(Ord. No. 2020-012, § 1, 9-28-2020)
212:
(a) Each applicant applying for a license shall attach to his application detailed plans of the building and outside premises. Sufficient detail shall be provided to show compliance with this article for the type of license requested. The building shall comply with all ordinances of the city, regulations of the state revenue commissioner and the laws of the state.
(b) Each applicant applying for a pouring license shall attach to his application evidence of ownership of the building or proposed building or a copy of the lease, if the applicant is leasing the building. No percentage leases of buildings or realty for pouring outlet stores shall be permitted.
(Ord. No. 2020-012, § 1, 9-28-2020)
213:
(a) Where a building in which any person intends to operate under the provisions of this chapter is, at the time of the application for the license, not in existence or not yet completed, a conditional license may be issued for the location, provided the plans for the proposed building show clearly a compliance with the other provisions of this chapter. No sales or consumption shall be allowed in the establishment until it has been completed in accordance with the plans and is in conformity with all of the other provisions of this Code.
(b) All licensees under this chapter must, within 90 days after the issuance of a city license, open for business. Failure to open for business shall constitute a forfeiture and cancellation of the issued license, and no refund of license fees or occupational taxes shall be made. Any applicant unable to comply with the time limit of this section may make written request to the administrator for an extension of time not to exceed 90 days; and the administrator, at his discretion, may grant or deny the request.
(Ord. No. 2020-012, § 1, 9-28-2020)
214:
(a) No retail package license shall be granted to any person unless the front door of the premises of the proposed location is situated not less than 100 yards from any church building, not less than 200 yards from the property line of any school grounds or college campus, and not less than 100 yards from any building used as an alcohol treatment center, the same to be measured by the most direct route of travel on the ground.
(b) No pouring license shall be granted to any person unless the front door of the premises of the proposed location is situated not less than 100 yards from any church building, not less than 200 yards from the property line of any school grounds or college campus, and not less than 100 yards from any building used as an alcohol treatment center, the same to be measured by the most direct route of travel on the ground.
(c) Each applicant for a package or pouring license shall include a scale drawing of the location of the proposed premises showing the distance to the nearest type of building and/or property lines of types of property referred to in O.C.G.A. § 3-3-21 and subsection (a) and (b) of this section, or a certificate of a registered surveyor that such location complies with such provisions.
(Ord. No. 2020-012, § 1, 9-28-2020)
215:
The parking area of any building in which alcoholic beverages are sold at retail package or pouring shall be paved with concrete or asphalt and contain sufficient square footage and parking spaces as required by ordinance for the type of business and building in which the business is to be operated.
(Ord. No. 2020-012, § 1, 9-28-2020)
216:
Each building in which alcoholic beverages are sold at retail or pouring shall contain sufficient lighting so that the building itself and the premises on all outside exposed walls of the building are readily visible at all times from the street on which the building is located so as to reveal the inside retail area of the building and so as to reveal all of the outside premises of the building.
(Ord. No. 2020-012, § 1, 9-28-2020)
217:
No licensed establishment selling or distributing distilled spirits or malt beverages and wine shall be located within the city except in the zoning districts as designated by the City of Emerson Zoning Ordinance.
(Ord. No. 2020-012, § 1, 9-28-2020)
218:
(a) It shall be unlawful for any pouring outlet, pouring licensee or any employee thereof to sell, pour or serve alcoholic beverages or allow any person to consume alcoholic beverages on the premises at any of the following times:
(1) At any time on Christmas Day.
(2) At any time in violation of a local ordinance or regulation or a special order of the governing authority.
(3) No pouring shall be permitted between the hours of 2:00 a.m. and 10:00 a.m., Monday through Saturday
(4) No alcoholic beverages may be consumed on the premises of the pouring outlet between the hours of 2:30 a.m. and 10:00 a.m., Monday through Saturday.
(5) No pouring shall be permitted between the hours of 2:00 a.m. and 11:00 a.m. on Sunday.
(6) No alcoholic beverages may be consumed on the premises of the pouring outlet between the hours of 2:30 a.m. and 11:00 a.m. on Sunday.
(7) In no event shall alcoholic beverages be sold, delivered or served during the prohibited hours, based upon timely sale of tickets, chips, decanters or other devices.
(b) A pouring outlet duly licensed, pouring licensee or any employee thereof shall only be permitted to sell, pour, or serve alcoholic beverages, or allow any person to consume alcoholic beverages on the premises during the following times:
(1) At any time not prohibited by section 4-194(a) as indicated in section 4-194(b).
(2) Pouring shall be permitted between the hours of 10:00 a.m. and 2:00 a.m., Monday through Saturday.
(3) Pouring shall be permitted between the hours of 11:00 a.m. and 2:00 a.m. on Sunday.
(4) Alcoholic beverages may be consumed on the premises between the hours of 10:00 a.m. and 2:30 a.m. Monday through Saturday.
(5) Alcoholic beverages may be consumed on the premises on Sunday between 11:00 a.m. and 2:30 a.m.
(Ord. No. 2020-012, § 1, 9-28-2020; Ord. No. 2026-002, § 1, 1-12-2026)
219:
It shall be unlawful for any person to sell or serve any malt beverage or wine on Christmas Day, or any day prior to 6:00 a.m. or after 12:00 midnight; furthermore, it shall be unlawful for any person to sell or serve any malt beverage or wine on Sunday prior to 12:30 p.m. or after 11:30 p.m.
(Ord. No. 2020-012, § 1, 9-28-2020)
222:
A license holder, before employing any person for the sale or handling of malt beverages or wine and distilled spirits shall submit such prospective employee's name and identification information to the Emerson Police Department, who shall make such investigation as he or she may deem necessary as to the qualification of such prospective employee before issuing a handler's permit for such person. available for photographing, fingerprinting and such other investigating as may be required by the city to the police department, who shall make such investigation as to such prospective employee's qualifications, before issuing such person an employee identification card.
(Ord. No. 2020-012, § 1, 9-28-2020)
223:
(a) An employee under this chapter must be and continue to be a person of a good moral character and must meet the following additional qualifications, which shall be required during the entire period that the employee is employed at the licensed establishment:
(1) The employee shall not have been convicted, within three years of the date of his application, of a felony or any violation of the laws of this state or any other state relating to the sale of alcoholic beverages.
(2) The employee shall not have had revoked, for cause, such as a violation of regulations or improper operation, within three years next preceding his employment, any license issued to him by any state, county, or municipality to sell alcoholic beverages. This subsection (a)(2) shall not apply to any licenses heretofore revoked by the city.
(3) The employee must be able to read and write the English language.
(4) The employee shall make a sworn statement of his qualifications under the provisions of this section, and shall place it on file with the city. Any misstatement or concealment of fact in the application shall be grounds for revocation of the license, and shall make the employee liable to prosecution for perjury under the laws of the state.
(b) A violation of any of the above qualifications and restrictions shall be grounds for suspension or revocation of the license issued.
(Ord. No. 2020-012, § 1, 9-28-2020)
224:
(a) Any person, including the licensee, who works in an establishment licensed under this chapter shall apply to the police department for an employee identification card, which card shall expire one year from the date issued, and be renewable on or before that time.
(b) Employees, while on duty in a pouring outlet or package wine outlet shop which provides wine samples, selling, pouring, serving alcoholic beverages or providing samples shall visibly wear the employee identification card on their persons at all times. All other employees must have the employee identification card at the facility while on duty.
(c) The police department shall investigate employee applicants. An employee identification card shall not be granted to any person who does not meet the requirements or qualifications of an employee as described in this chapter. The police department shall report any other detrimental information about an application to the city, and may prohibit the issuance of an employee identification card where the applicant's record indicates such employment would adversely affect the public health, safety or welfare, or violate the law.
(d) No licensee under the provisions of this chapter shall hire any person, nor shall any person work or assist in an establishment licensed under this chapter, until such person has procured an employee identification card.
(e) The police department may provisionally grant identification to an applicant, pending investigation and report. Where the report, when reviewed, is unfavorable as set out in subsection (c) of this section, the police department may revoke the card and demand its return.
(f) The city may, after reasonable notice and hearing (unless waived), revoke an identification card and demand its surrender where the employee violates the provisions of this article, or becomes one who adversely affects the public health, safety and welfare.
(g) It shall be unlawful for an employee whose card has been revoked, and upon whom demand for surrender of a card has been made, to refuse to so surrender, or to alter, conceal, deface or destroy the card.
(Ord. No. 2020-012, § 1, 9-28-2020)
225:
No pouring licensee shall employ, require or permit persons less than 18 years of age to sell, pour, serve or take orders for any alcoholic beverages.
(Ord. No. 2020-012, § 1, 9-28-2020)
228:
(a) In addition to the requirements of this chapter, a license for the distilled spirits package upon the terms and conditions provided in this article shall be granted by the city council and evidenced by a written approval executed by the majority of the members of the city council. Upon the compliance with the foregoing provision and at the direction of the city council, the city manager or his/her designee shall issue a distilled spirits package license.
(b) No owner shall hold more than one approved distilled spirits package license.
(c) A licensee of a distilled spirits package establishment under this article shall not operate the business in connection with any other mercantile establishment, provided, this shall not prohibit a retail spirituous liquor licensee from operating in the same building complex with other businesses.
(Ord. No. 2023-007, 3-27-2023; Ord. No. 2023-023, 11-13-2023)
229:
Distilled spirits package licensees shall store all alcoholic beverages on the premises for which the license was issued and at no other place. All stock shall be available at all times for inspection by any duly authorized representative of the city. Any alcoholic beverages found in any licensee's stock which was not sold or distributed in accordance with laws of the state to make sales and deliveries in the city shall be deemed contraband and subject to immediate confiscation.
(Ord. No. 2023-007, 3-27-2023; Ord. No. 2023-023, 11-13-2023)
230:
Retail dealers in distilled spirits licensed under the applicable provisions of this chapter shall not buy nor accept deliveries of distilled spirits from wholesalers or other persons offering distilled spirits for sale except from wholesalers duly licensed under this chapter. Such retail dealers shall only accept deliveries of distilled spirits directly to the premises for which their license and permit was issued, and by no means other than a conveyance owned and operated by a wholesaler licensed as required by this chapter; except that, on written request to the city manager and upon the granting of permission by the city in writing, deliveries may in special instances be made otherwise upon terms and conditions as prescribed by the city as to each delivery.
(Ord. No. 2023-007, 3-27-2023; Ord. No. 2023-023, 11-13-2023)
231:
No distilled spirits package shall be sold at retail except in establishments located in the zoning districts C-1, C-2, or MU-2.
(Ord. No. 2023-007, 3-27-2023; Ord. No. 2023-023, 11-13-2023)
232:
For licensees who wish to operate a business which conducts both the retail sale of distilled spirits package and the retail sale of package malt beverages and wine, in the case of conflict, the provisions of this article regulating the retail sale of distilled spirits package shall prevail, and compliance with those provisions, rather than the provisions applicable to the license permitting the retail sale of package malt beverages and wine, is required.
(Ord. No. 2023-007, 3-27-2023; Ord. No. 2023-023, 11-13-2023)
233:
(a) No distilled spirits package license shall be granted to any person unless the requirements as to location and distance are in compliance with O.C.G.A. § 3-3-21.
(b) Applicants for a distilled spirits package license shall include with their application, a scaled drawing providing evidence that all of the locational requirements listed in this division have been met. Such applications shall be reviewed by the City of Emerson for compliance with all distance requirements.
(c) Distilled spirits package stores must operate as sole tenants in at least 2,000 square feet in size.
(d) A distilled spirits package store shall not be located closer than 1,500 feet to another distilled spirits package store, regardless of jurisdiction as measured from door to door along street right-of-way by the most direct route.
(e) Distilled spirits package store deliveries shall be made at the side or rear of the store building and all loading areas, dumpsters, recycling bins, and compactors shall be screened from ground view.
(f) Distilled spirits package store properties shall have no outdoor storage including the storage of shopping carts.
(g) Distilled spirits package stores shall have no drive-through window.
(h) All glass surfaces forming the exterior walls of the premises shall remain unobstructed and shall provide a clear line of sight into the interior of the premises that is licensed to sell distilled spirits package and no signs, window coverings, or other material shall be placed on or within ten feet of any exterior glass surfaces, except as follows:
(1) One "open" sign which includes business hours of operation, and which may be illuminated, not to exceed four and one-half square feet in area. Any additional signs on the property and premises shall also comply with all applicable provisions of the City of Emerson's sign ordinance.
(i) All distilled spirits package stores shall be within a building or room totally physically separate from any other business activities. The only ingress and egress for customers and their purchases shall be through a door opening to the outside or to an area for public pedestrian traffic and not from or into any other business establishment. This outside door shall open facing a public street or public pedestrian area.
(j) Any opening of any type shall be prohibited between any area licensed as a distilled spirit package store and any other business area. The only means of ingress and egress for both customer and employee shall be through a door open to the outside and facing a public street or public pedestrian area.
(k) In a distilled spirits package store, the total commercial transactions shall take place within the area licensed for retail alcoholic package sales.
(l) No licensee for the sale of distilled spirits by the package shall operate under the license, unless the front entrance to the licensed premises is clearly visible from the public street; provided, however, that this restriction shall not apply where the licensee is a motel, hotel, private club or is located in shopping center or multiple-story business building.
(m) Not less than 60 percent of the front retail area shall be glass. Front retail area shall mean the width of the area used for retail sales of the premises from the ceiling to the floor.
(n) No screens, blinds, curtains, partitions, articles or things which shall prevent a clear view into the interior shall be permitted in the window or from the doors of any distilled spirits package store; and no booth, screen, partition or other obstruction shall be permitted within the interior of any such store. Each store shall be so lighted that the interior of the store is visible day and night.
(o) No license shall be issued for the operation of any distilled spirits package store on the premises of any establishment licensed and operating self-service motor fuel dispensing pumps.
(Ord. No. 2023-007, 3-27-2023; Ord. No. 2023-023, 11-13-2023; Ord. No. 2024-008, 4-22-2024)
234:
(a) Retail package licensees shall not engage in the sale of distilled spirits except between the hours of 7:00 a.m. and 11:45 p.m., Monday through Saturday, and 12:00 p.m. until 11:45 p.m. on Sundays. The hours within which business may be carried on shall be determined by the standard time in force at the time of the sale thereof.
(b) Retail distilled spirits package shall not be sold at any time in violation of any local ordinance or regulations or of any special order of the governing authority.
(Ord. No. 2023-007, 3-27-2023; Ord. No. 2023-023, 11-13-2023)
235:
It shall be unlawful for any person to consume any alcoholic beverage on a premises licensed for the sale of distilled spirits package. For the purpose of this section, the term "premises" shall include the parking area immediately adjoining the premises licensed for the sale of distilled spirits package and available for the use of the customers of the licensed premises, whether or not the same are owned or leased by the licensed holder. It shall be unlawful for any licensee to permit the consumption of alcoholic beverages on said premises or to sell unsealed (broken) distilled spirits package.
(Ord. No. 2023-007, 3-27-2023; Ord. No. 2023-023, 11-13-2023)
236:
Retailers shall indicate plainly by tags or labels on the bottles or containers or on the shelf immediately below where the containers are placed the prices of all distilled spirits exposed or offered for sale.
(Ord. No. 2023-007, 3-27-2023; Ord. No. 2023-023, 11-13-2023)
238:
(a) Any tasting event shall be held on the premises of the distilled spirits package store and must comply with the requirements of O.C.G.A. § 3-15-2.
(Ord. No. 2023-007, 3-27-2023; Ord. No. 2023-023, 11-13-2023)
239:
No licensee, nor any agent or employee of the licensee, nor any other person shall do any of the following upon the licensed premises. No licensee shall:
(1) Sell or deliver any alcohol to any person except in the licensee's place of business.
(2) Furnish, sell or offer for sale any alcohol before 12:00 p.m. on Sundays or after 11:45 p.m. on Sundays.
(3) Sell or possess for sale any alcohol where such person does not have a license to sell or possess for sale.
(4) Receive alcohol at the premises other than by a wholesale dealer with a permit granted by the city.
(5) Knowingly and intentionally offer for sale, sell, barter, exchange, give, provide or furnish alcohol to any person confined in any jail, penal institution, correctional facility, prison camp, penitentiary or other lawful place of confinement, or to any person who is noticeably intoxicated, or who is of unsound mind, or is a habitual drunkard whose intemperate habits are known to the licensee.
(6) Fail to post in a conspicuous place in the licensed premises the signs required by this chapter and state law.
(7) Fail to maintain on the licensed premises at all times a telephone in good working order.

(a) Purpose. The purpose of this chapter is to define false alarm, to make the activation of an alarm system or placement of a telephone call to report an emergency when there is no emergency a violation of the ordinance from which this article is derived, to establish penalties for initiating a false alarm, and related items.
(b) Definitions. The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this article, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this subsection, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
Alarm means any signal (audio or video, recorded or live) transmitted to the county, indicating a predetermined emergency condition exists, when the alarm is received by:
(1) The county 911 communications center or the city's telephone;
(2) A private alarm service company relaying the alarm to the county 911 communications center or the city's telephone; or
(3) An automated telephone alarm system, playing a recorded message when received at the county 911 communications center or the city's telephone.
Additionally, the term "alarm" means any audible or visual sign or signal received by the county 911 communications center or the city's telephone.
Alarm system means an assembly of equipment and devices designed and arranged to detect a fire or signal an unauthorized intrusion onto premises, or attempted robbery at protected premises, or other emergency situation, and, with respect to said signal, public safety officers are expected to respond.
False alarm means the activation of an alarm system when none of the emergency situations for which the alarm system has been installed have, in fact, occurred. This includes the accidental activation of an alarm by the property owner, premises lessee, resident or tenant.
Telephone alarm system means any alarm system which automatically transmits by telephone line a recorded electronic or mechanical signal to a telephonic instrument located at the county 911 communications center or offices of the city. A telephone alarm system is prohibited.
(c) Unlawful activation; failure to notify police department of malfunctioning alarm system when reporting an activated alarm. It is unlawful for anyone to activate any fire, robbery or burglar alarm for the purpose of summoning public safety officers except in the event of an actual fire, attempted burglary or robbery or other emergency. It is unlawful for anyone to notify the police department or the fire department of an activated alarm when that person knows that activation of the alarm was caused by a malfunction of the alarm system or by maintenance or repair work on the alarm system without simultaneously telling the police department about the malfunction or maintenance or repair.
(d) Response to false alarm; fees; corrective action.
(1) For each response to a false alarm, the property owner or premises lessee shall, within five business days, provide a written explanation to the city's police department describing the reasons for the false alarm.
(2) Upon receipt of the explanation, the police department may take the following actions:
a. For the first false alarm from a premises within a three-month period, leave an alarm response notice and a copy of the ordinance from which this article is derived at the premises (on or under the main or front door). The notice shall include information that continued false alarms will lead to a service charge.
b. For the second false alarm from a premises within a three-month period, inform the property owner or premises lessee that the alarm system should be inspected by a state-licensed contractor and corrective measures taken. The property owner or premises lessee is responsible for payment of such inspection and/or repair.
c. For the third false alarm from a premises within a three-month period, charge the property owner or premises lessee a fee established by the city.
d. For the fourth false alarm from a premises within a three-month period and for each subsequent false alarm from a premises within a three-month period, charge the property owner or premises lessee a fee established by the city.
(3) Civil penalties. Violations of any provision of this article shall be enforced through the assessment of civil penalty(ies) as maintained in the City of Emerson Fee Schedule.
(4) Exceptions.
a. The police department shall have the discretion to waive assessment of the fee if:
1. The false alarm was activated by inclement weather; or
2. Within ten days of the occurrence of a false alarm, the property owner or premises lessee demonstrates that the alarm system has been examined by an authorized repair service and the repair service certifies that the alarm system now works correctly.
b. Notwithstanding the foregoing in this subsection (4), within a three-month period, only one such explanation from the property owner or premises lessee shall be accepted as the basis for avoiding a fee assessment.
(5) Payment of civil penalties. Civil penalties shall be paid within 30 days from the date of the invoice from the city.
(6) Noncriminal (civil) violation. A violation of any of the provision of this division shall be civil in nature and shall not constitute a misdemeanor or infraction.
(7) Appeals process. Assessments of civil penalties and other enforcement decisions made under this division may be appealed by filing a written notice of appeal with the police chief, as applicable, within 30 days after the date of notification of the assessment of civil penalties or other enforcement decisions. The written notice of appeal shall contain the cause for the appeal and any other pertinent information relevant to the case. The failure to give notice of appeal within this time period shall constitute a waiver of the right to consent the assessment of penalties or other enforcement decisions. The police chief shall designate a hearing officer from the police department to hear appeals related to their agency. The respective hearing officer shall render a decision within five business days and give written notification of his/her decision. The hearing officer's decision may be appealed to the chief of police by filing a written notice of appeal within ten days of receipt of the hearing officer's decision. The chief of police shall have the final decision in this matter. The hearing officer's decision and the decision of the respective chief are subject to review by the courts having jurisdiction by proceeding in the nature of writ of certiorari.
(8) Appeal standard. The hearing officer shall review an appeal from the assessment of civil penalties or other enforcement decisions using a preponderance of the evidence standard. Notwithstanding a determination that the preponderance of the evidence supports the assessment of civil penalties or other enforcement decision, the hearing officer shall have the discretion to dismiss or reduce civil penalties or reverse any other enforcement decision where warranted.
(9) Responsibility for fees/costs. In the event the appeal is not upheld, the owner or lessee shall also be responsible for any fee assessed to reimburse the city for any costs incurred by the hearing officer in enforcing this article.
(Ord. of 8-27-2007(1), §§ 1—3; Ord. No. 2020-011, § 1, 9-28-2020)

(a) Title. This chapter shall be known as the "City of Emerson Fire Hydrant Ordinance."
(b) Purpose. The purpose of this chapter is to provide a standard system for hydrant color identification and establish a practice of maintenance for fire hydrants within the service area of the county fire department, which includes the incorporated areas of the city. These provisions shall incorporate by reference the American Water Works Association (AWWA) manual M17, "Installation, Field Testing, and Maintenance of Fire Hydrants;" the National Fire Protection Association (NFPA) 291 latest edition, defining fire flow testing and marking hydrants; and the Insurance Service Organization (ISO) standards for fire hydrant testing, collectively referred to herein as the "standards."
(c) Testing required. All fire hydrants within the service area of the county fire department and owned by the water system of the city shall be flowed and tested in accordance with the standards. The testing shall determine the gallons per minute (GPM) fire flow for that hydrant. Testing shall be coordinated with the water system. Proper public notice shall be issued in advance of any testing to ensure the public is aware of potential water discoloration.
(d) Color coding. After testing, each hydrant shall then be color coded in accordance with NFPA 291, as follows:
(1) Standard hydrants.
| GMP Flow Rate | Paint Color
Barrels | Any | Safety yellow
Bonnets and caps | Less than 500 | Safety red
| 500 to 999 | Safety orange
| 1,000 to 1,499 | Safety green
| 1,500 or greater | Safety blue
Trim of bonnet | Any | Silver or white reflective (if available)
Disclaimer: Color coding is only descriptive of what GPM flow was at the time of the last documented test. It in no way guarantees that the hydrant will flow at that GPM rate at the time of an incident and does not take into account any high demands, broken mains, closed valves or other events that could affect GPM flow. Color coding is only used as a general reference to what the potential flow may be at any given time, and citizens and staff should be aware and prepared for GPM flow changes.
(2) Special hydrants.
Bastard thread hydrant (non-NST) | Caps—Gloss black
Private hydrant | Barrel, bonnet and caps—Solid red
Out-of-service hydrant | Barrel, bonnet and caps—Safety yellow or clearly marked with a covering to identify out-of-service status.
(e) Maintenance procedures. An annual maintenance schedule and visual check program shall be established by the county fire department. Personnel and citizen safety shall be a high priority. All fire hydrants are to be opened and closed very slowly to prevent water hammer, line damage and equipment failure.
(f) Recording data. All test data shall be maintained in the county fire department records as well as the records of the city's water system. A record of malfunctions, corrections and system changes shall be recorded. Any malfunction of the system, while performing work on the system, is to be immediately reported to the battalion chief, who will in turn notify appropriate water system officials.
(Ord. No. 2014-018, §§ 1-1, 1-2, 9-22-2014)
